title: Next Step of Advanced RAIM for Rail, Maritime and UAS Sectors
description: In this action the contractor shall support the standardisation and dissemination activities conducted by the European Commission and EUSPA on Advance RAIM in sectors beyond Aviation and shall perform safety and cost benefit analyses for the use of ARAIM in those other sectors.The contractor shall also collect real measurements and validate local effect models. Evolutions of ARAIM shall be developed considering combination with the following technologies and services:— multi-sensor fusion, a required evolution of GNSS and ARAIM since autonomous transportation in most safety critical sectors rely on local sensors able to mitigate the effects of local errors and signal masking in harsh environment;— EGNOS current and future versions, which will augment GPS and Galileo in the L1 and L5 bands and will extend the service area;— Galileo High Accuracy Service (HAS) that will improve positioning performance through the E6-B signal and by terrestrial means.

title: EU Complementary Time (C-T) and Complementary Position and Navigation (C-PN) services
description:
Satellite-based navigation and timing services are a cornerstone of Europe’s economy and critical infrastructure resilience. Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) functions, delivered principally by Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) such as the EU owned Galileo, underpin sectors ranging from transport and finance to energy and telecommunications. Several studies attribute roughly 10 % of EU GDP to PNT related activities, while a single day without GNSS could have a financial impact up to €1 billion.
The Commission proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), includes for the 2028‑2034 Multi‑annual Financial Framework, a contribution to complementary PNT services, which shall increase the resilience in case of disruptions to the services provided by the PNT component (Article 59).
The project shall assess how best can the Commission contribute to complementary PNT services in the next MFF.
Leveraging existing national and pan‑European infrastructure, the Commission would like to assess:
•	How to best strengthen with the resilience of PNT services to radio frequency interference (RFI) affecting GNSS services throughout the EU.
•	How to best contribute to the deployment of a mature, interoperable C T architecture that is ready for operational use within the multi financial framework 2028 2034.
•	How to best support candidates for a C-PN service, that utilise the C-T infrastructure and are resilient to RFI and to assess whether the technology is ready for deployment or, if not what is required.

title: Fused PNT Analyses based on European Infrastructure
description:
The European Commission is launching a study on the potential use of communication-oriented LEO constellations for the deployment of a complementary PNT service. This approach is normally referred to as Fused PNT.
This tender will focus on developing a user terminal prototype and a simulated environment enabling to assess the performance of Fused PNT under a realistic set of propagation conditions and inter-satellite interference. In this procurement, the main goals of the European Commission are: 
• To develop a software receiver, supporting acquisition and tracking of 3GPP reference signals for Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) 
• To model multipath channel and intersatellite interference, in order to test the software receiver under the realistic satellite based propagation channel and interferences;
• To consolidate and complement the part of the E2E emulator, by adding multipath and intersatellite interference models; 
• To demonstrate the performance of fused PNT ranging in a representative simulated environment 
• To validate the acquisition and tracking performance in realistic environment.

title: EU integrated Multi-constellation and Multi-sensor Radio Frequency Interference Monitoring system - M2RFI, GNSS
description:
This project aims to explore the concept of diversifying RF Interference (RFI) monitoring beyond sole reliance on a single space-based infrastructure or sensor type, instead leveraging the potential of accessing and combining multiple satellite constellations and diverse data from heterogeneous data sources. Integrating multiple space-based systems could be a cost-effective alternative to deploying a large constellation of satellites, which would be required to achieve high resolution and widespread coverage. 

The primary outcome of the project will be the definition of an optimal algorithm, tailored to specific use cases, which will aggregate and processing diverse input RFI data and best comply to mission requirements.

title: GNSS RFI on-board
description:
The subject of this call for tenders is to demonstrate the feasibility of implementing the most promising and mature On-board Resilience Techniques against GNSS Frequency Jamming and Spoofing in a GNSS Receiver Prototype or Demonstrator (hardware and/or software). The objective is to get this Receiver Prototype/Demonstrator to, as a minimum, a Technology Readiness Level of TRL4 (technology validated in lab) or TRL5 (technology validated in relevant environment) , or higher if possible, taking into account the state of the art in the science and applications of navigation.
Additionally, it is also an objective to perform some technological studies to better support future developments: Assess which are the optimal complementary technologies depending on the domain; Assess the GNSS receiver behaviour in the presence of an RFI event and Assess the possibility of including the results of the implementation of the On-board GNSS Resilience Techniques in a real receiver.
